key_findings: Obtained full text of LeBoeuf & Simmons (2010, JMR) via author-hosted OA copy (Wharton faculty platform).

Independently re-computed Study 4's headline statistics from the paper's published aggregate data (Table 6): mismatch~evaluation r=0.502 (paper r=.50, p=.003); category-function~evaluation r=-0.015 (paper -.01, p=.94); advertisement-function~evaluation r=-0.496 (paper -.50, p=.004); partial r=.166/p=.372 (paper .17/.37) and r=-.141/p=.450 (paper -.14/.45); utilitarian vs symbolic ad means 4.18 vs 4.54 (paper 4.18 vs 4.55). All match to rounding.
Confirmed internal arithmetic consistency of Table 1 (Study 1a), Table 4 (Study 2a) and Table 5 (Study 2b) cell means/averages.

Could NOT obtain or re-run the raw reproduction data/scripts (Somo et al. 2020 computational reproduction) because the OSF platform was in emergency maintenance for the entire audit window (API returned maintenance-mode 503 across sustained polling). Thus Studies 1-3 t-tests/ANOVAs (H1, H2, H3) could not be independently re-run.

Human FLoRA registry verdict for this study = 'computationally reproducible'; a FORRT-recorded computational reproduction (Somo et al. 2020) exists. We found no contradiction but could not end-to-end confirm due to OSF outage.
notes: Study 4 headline correlation claim verified EXACTLY from published aggregate data. Studies 1-3 headline claims (branding alters attitude functions; function-matching advantage attenuated at brand level) NOT independently re-run because raw data/scripts are hosted on OSF, which was in prolonged maintenance mode (centre for open science status: emergency maintenance + scheduled 20:00-22:00 EDT window) throughout the audit. Data_status=partial: paper + published aggregates reproduced; reproduction dataset not obtained. Verdict is PARTIAL, not NODATA or FAIL; consistent with the human 'computationally reproducible' rating (no deviations found).
